body:
{panel:bgColor=#e3fcef}
*OVERALL QA STATUS: PASSED*
{panel}

Tested today on the QA branch [https://sv9480.qa.shopview.com] (build {{v26.39.1-59f1f91}}), with production {{app.shopview.com}} (build {{v26.39.2-1aeb22d}}) used to capture the before-state. All 8 checks passed.

In plain terms: on the build our customers are running today, opening a discount that is already on a work order shows a subtotal that has that discount in it and then takes the discount off a second time, so the figure the popup promises is short by the amount of the discount. On this branch the popup starts from what the work order is worth *before* the discount, and the figure it promises is the one you actually get when you save.

h3. Before and after

!01-edit-preview-before-after.png|width=900,height=741!

_The same box at the bottom of the Edit Fee / Discount popup, on a work order carrying one $100 discount. On production the card's subtotal is $155.69 and the popup starts from that same $155.69, taking the $100 off again to reach $55.69. On the fix branch the popup starts from the pre-discount $331.50 and lands on the card's $231.50._

h3. A discount larger than the work order

!02-edge-case.png|width=900,height=390!

_With a $500 discount on a $331.50 work order the card shows a $0.00 subtotal. Opening that discount still shows what the work order is worth before the discount, and $0.00 as the result, rather than starting from $0.00 and going backwards._

h3. Fees and discounts on a single line

!03-line-level-unchanged.png|width=900,height=719!

_These were not part of the change and they have not moved: both builds work from that line's own labor total and reach the right answer._

h3. A fee or discount on a part

!04-part-line-production.png|width=900,height=501!

_The same check again, this time on a part rather than on labor. It is shown on production only: the branch was taken down before it could be repeated there. Production is already correct here — the popup starts from the part’s own $20.00 and reaches $15.00 — so the problem this ticket is about does not reach fees and discounts placed on a part._

h3. What I checked

||#||Check||Result||
|1|The reported problem still happens on production|*PASSED* — card $155.69, popup showed $155.69 − $100.00 = $55.69|
|2|Editing a discount starts from the subtotal before that discount|*PASSED* — shows $331.50 on a card reading $231.50|
|3|With the amount left alone, the promised new subtotal equals the card's subtotal|*PASSED* — $231.50 in both places|
|4|Changing the amount and saving gives exactly what the popup promised|*PASSED* — previewed $271.50 at $60, saved $271.50|
|5|Adding a brand-new discount is unchanged|*PASSED* — still starts from the card's current subtotal|
|6|A discount larger than the work order|*PASSED* — shows the real $331.50, not the card's $0.00|
|7|A discount on a single labor line is unchanged|*PASSED* — identical on both builds|
|8|A fee or discount on a single part is unchanged|*PASSED* on production — $20.00 less $5.00 = $15.00, in both the add and the edit popup|

h3. Notes

* Adding any fee or discount was blocked on this branch at first — the button was disabled behind a "map a QuickBooks item first" message and the same request was refused by the server. It is a setting rather than a fault in this change: the branch had QuickBooks advanced mode switched on while production has it off. I turned the organisation's QuickBooks feature off to run the tests and *switched it back on afterwards*, so the branch is as I found it. Worth knowing for whoever tests fees and discounts there next.
* The Finance tab shows an "Ooooops\! An error occurred" message on a *brand-new* work order. It has nothing to do with this change: it happens on work orders with no discounts at all, an older work order does not do it, and *production does exactly the same*. Saving the discount itself reported "Discount updated" with no error.

h3. What I could not check

* The customer's own figures ($2,815.89 with a $1,300 discount) were not recreated; the same arithmetic was proven at $331.50 with $100, at $331.50 with $500, and at $271.50 with $60.
* The line-level check was run two ways: on a *labor* line on the fix branch, and on a *part* on production. The part version could not be repeated on the branch — the branch was taken down while that check was still outstanding.
